newsitem.title: USA: Conn. residents see rosy economic future - poll.
newsitem.headline: Conn. residents see rosy economic future - poll.

text.p: Connecticut residents feel more upbeat about their personal finances and the country's economic future than at any time since 1990, the Hartford Courant reported Tuesday in a poll it sponsored.
The so-called Gross National Spirit Index, measured by the University of Connecticut's Institute for Social Inquiry, has been conducted twice a year since 1981.

The latest sampling found that Nutmeg State residents feel pretty good about their personal situations and finances, the president, the country's economic prospects and the way things are going in general in the U.S. today.
Of the 500 randomly selected state residents, 69 percent said they were "more or less satisfied" with the way things are going in the U.S. today.
Some 79 percent said they were satisfied with their family's financial situation, and 30 percent believe the U.S. economy will improve next year.
Only 25 percent said they disapproved of Bill Clinton's performance as president.

"What the poll suggests is that people's perceptions of the way things are going, on a variety of dimensions, are really optimistic, more optimistic than they've been in the recent past," poll director G. Donald Ferree Jr. was quoted in the Courant as saying.
The latest cheerful findings still fall short of the poll's alltime peak in December 1983. The Gross National Spirit survey weighed in higher eight times during the Reagan administration.
